native_mechanisms: A single rolling sphere is the only carried memory across the whole ordered pile (one accumulator, streamed in order, old state discarded)

Each mark is pressed into the sphere and then tumbled a fixed count of turns down the trail, the strike on a stalk cracking it, before the next mark is taken (add the word, then rotate by a fixed pitch, then a crack/shift at the stalk — mixing by turns and strikes, never by multiplication)

Only the final hairline crack in the last stalk is handed over; the sphere itself, all intermediate cracks and dust are swept away (a strong one-shot finalisation is the output, intermediate states never emitted)
core_technique: Multiplication-free ARX streaming hash: each 8-byte word is added into one 64-bit accumulator which is then rotated by a fixed per-lane constant (add-rotate), with an xor-shift after each 32/8-byte group, finished by a bijective rotate/add/xor-shift + 32-bit-half ARX grind avalanche.
